# Borderless Window 1.11.0

*NeoForge · Fabric 26.2 · 2026-11-11*

> **Now on Minecraft 26.2.** Every feature of 1.11.0, on both loaders, with nothing else to install. With Iris shaders on, the zoom's Hide Hand and the separate Hand Bobbing now work too.

## ⚠️ Important Notes

- **The first version for Minecraft 26.2.** Download the file for 26.2 and your loader; the 26.1.2 and 1.21.x jars do not work here
- **Fullscreen is always exclusive with OpenGL**, as on 26.1.2: Minecraft's "Exclusive Fullscreen" option stays hidden from Video Settings, since the Screen Mode selector already covers both kinds of fullscreen. **With Vulkan** (Minecraft 26.2's new Graphics API option), Minecraft's fullscreen is never exclusive, whatever the mod or that option does, so Fullscreen there does not conflict with HDR. Borderless is still the one to use with HDR or for instant Alt+Tab on OpenGL
- **If you type with a Chinese, Japanese or Korean input method**, use Borderless instead of Fullscreen. Sodium keeps Minecraft's fullscreen non-exclusive for those input methods, and Borderless works better with them
- **Vulkan on NeoForge:** NeoForge 26.2.0.93's early loading screen always opens an OpenGL window, so with Graphics API on Vulkan the game stops at launch with "GLFW error 65540". This is a NeoForge issue; until it is fixed, set `earlyWindowControl = false` in `config/fml.toml`. Fabric is not affected
- **Sodium integration needs Sodium 0.9.0 or newer**, as on 26.1.2
- Same config file and option IDs as on 1.21.x and 26.1.2: copying `config/borderlesswindow.json` from an older instance carries your settings over

## ✨ New Features

- **Everything from 1.11.0, on Minecraft 26.2**: the three screen modes and configurable F11, the FPS counter, the background options with the idle limit in two steps, the fog toggles and Fog Start, cloud height, sky and weather, the held item name, screen and camera overlays, split FOV, distortion and view bobbing, zoom, enchantment numerals, draw distances, and Minecraft's own sliders that Sodium leaves out
- **Iris support for the hand settings:** with a shaderpack on, Iris draws the hand itself, so Hide Hand While Zooming and Hand Bobbing used to have no effect. Both now work with shaders as well
- **The mod's icon** next to its name in Sodium's page list, as Sodium, Iris and Reese's Sodium Options show theirs
- **Links to the mod's page:** NeoForge's mod list now shows the button to its GitHub page, and the Website button in Mod Menu on Fabric works (it was greyed out)
- **Borderless now renders at exactly the monitor's resolution** (1920×1080 on a 1080p monitor, as F3 shows). Before, the picture was one row taller than the monitor and that row was hidden below the screen

## 🔧 Technical Changes

- Ported to Minecraft 26.2. Every hook was checked against the 26.2 code on both loaders:
  - **HUD**: Minecraft 26.2 moved the HUD out of `Gui` into a new `Hud` class, so the overlay, held item name and FPS counter hooks follow it. Hide HUD While Zooming now flips the HUD's own hidden state (F1 is no longer `options.hideGui`) around one frame and puts it back, so F1 stays as you left it and the hand and screen effects are not hidden with it
  - **Pause Rendering When Minimized**: the game now presents through its window surface and already skips copying and presenting while minimized; the mod skips extracting and drawing the frame
  - **Fullscreen**: Minecraft sets its fullscreen hint in its constructor now, once for each graphics API it tries; the mod forces it off there
  - **Borderless**: Minecraft 26.2 takes 1 px off the picture of a non-exclusive fullscreen window, which is 1 px taller than the monitor, as the mod's Borderless is. The mod ties that to its Borderless mode instead of Minecraft's fullscreen flag, which it no longer follows. Switching between Borderless and Fullscreen on the same monitor also reports the size change, which Minecraft would otherwise miss

# Borderless Window 1.11.0

*NeoForge · Fabric 26.1.2 · 2026-11-11*

> **Now on Minecraft 26.1.2.** Every feature of 1.11.0, on both loaders, with nothing else to install, and a Fullscreen mode that is always exclusive.

## ⚠️ Important Notes

- **The first version for Minecraft 26.1.2.** Download the file for 26.1.2 and your loader; the 1.21.x jars do not work here
- **Fullscreen is always exclusive.** Minecraft 26.1 added its own "Exclusive Fullscreen" option, off by default. Off, Minecraft's fullscreen is not really exclusive: it stays on top of everything and still minimizes when you Alt+Tab, a weaker version of Borderless. Sodium turns that option on at first launch, so the same Fullscreen behaved differently with and without Sodium. Now the mod's Fullscreen is exclusive either way, and Minecraft's option is hidden from Video Settings, since the Screen Mode selector already covers both kinds of fullscreen. Borderless is still the one to use with HDR or for instant Alt+Tab
- **If you type with a Chinese, Japanese or Korean input method**, use Borderless instead of Fullscreen. Sodium keeps Minecraft's fullscreen non-exclusive for those input methods, and Borderless works better with them
- **Sodium integration needs Sodium 0.9.0 or newer.** Sodium's 26.1 builds replaced its Fullscreen checkbox with a "Fullscreen Mode" selector (Off / Exclusive / Borderless); the mod's Screen Mode takes its place, as it did with the checkbox
- Same config file and option IDs as on 1.21.x: copying `config/borderlesswindow.json` from an older instance carries your settings over

## ✨ New Features

- **Everything from 1.11.0, on Minecraft 26.1.2**: the three screen modes and configurable F11, the FPS counter, the background options with the idle limit in two steps, the fog toggles and Fog Start, cloud height, sky and weather, the held item name, screen and camera overlays, split FOV, distortion and view bobbing, zoom, enchantment numerals, draw distances, and Minecraft's own sliders that Sodium leaves out
- With Sodium, the mod's six pages and the Screen Mode selector work as on 1.21.11, also alongside Reese's Sodium Options and Iris

## 🔧 Technical Changes

- Ported to Minecraft 26.1.2, which ships unobfuscated, runs on Java 25 and splits every frame into update, extract and render. Every hook was checked against the 26.1.2 code on both loaders:
  - **Zoom and Fluid FOV**: the camera now works out its own FOV, so both live in `Camera` (`calculateFov` and `modifyFovBasedOnDeathOrFluid`). The zoom still applies last, after NeoForge's ComputeFov event
  - **Pause Rendering When Minimized**: skips extracting, drawing and presenting the frame in `Minecraft.renderFrame`
  - **Weather**: empties the rain and snow columns of the weather render state. Skipping the draw call, as before, now crashes on an empty buffer
  - **Fog**: the same hook, now on the `FogData` that `FogRenderer.setupFog` returns
  - **Unfocused volume**: follows the window's own focus callback (`Window.onFocus`), which also counts clicking back in as activity for the idle limit
  - **HUD, overlays and screens**: on Minecraft's renamed extract methods (`GuiGraphicsExtractor`)
- **Fullscreen**: Minecraft's option only sets a GLFW hint (`GLFW_SOFT_FULLSCREEN`, from LWJGL's own GLFW) when the game starts. On Windows that hint just makes the window 1 px taller than the monitor so it is not taken over as exclusive. The mod forces it off in `GLX._initGlfw`; GLFW reads it each time it fits a window to a monitor, so it covers every switch to Fullscreen without a restart
- **On Fabric**, the bundled key binding module is now `fabric-key-mapping-api-v1`, renamed in 26.1, and the mod jar is no longer remapped. Fabric API is still not required
- **Fixed:** the title of the mod's config screen (without Sodium) was not drawn. Since Minecraft 1.21.6 text with a fully transparent color is skipped, and the title's white had no alpha

# Borderless Window 1.11.0 *NeoForge · Fabric 1.21.11 · 2026-11-10* > **A second step for the idle limit, which now takes over from Minecraft's.** Step away for a few minutes and the game drops to one frame rate; stay away longer and it drops further. Any key or mouse movement brings it all back at once. ## ⚠️ Important Notes - **While the mod's Idle FPS Limit is on, it replaces Minecraft's "AFK" mode** of Reduce FPS When (in Video Settings, or on Sodium's Performance page). Until now the two stacked and the lowest won, so a 20 FPS idle limit still ended up at 10 after ten minutes. Now the mod's idle limits are the only ones that apply, and Minecraft's 10 FPS while minimized stays. With the mod's Idle FPS Limit off (the default), Minecraft's option works exactly as before. The option itself keeps your choice; nothing is changed in `options.txt` - Every setting stays as it was. The new options start off - When updating, delete the 1.10.0 jar from your mods folder ## ✨ New Features ### Idle FPS limit in two steps - **Second Idle Limit After** and **Second Idle FPS Limit**: a later cap on top of the existing idle limit. For example, 30 FPS after 5 minutes without input, then 10 FPS after 20 minutes - The second time can go up to 60 minutes, and it is always longer than the first: its slider starts right after the first idle time, and its leftmost position is Off. Both times count from your last keyboard or mouse input - It builds on the first step, so it is greyed out while the first idle limit is off. # Borderless Window 1.10.0

*NeoForge · Fabric 1.21.1 · 2026-11-09*

> **Zoom, and a few details from OptiFine.** Press C to get a closer look, with the mouse wheel to go further. Plus: hide the sun, moon, stars, rain and snow, choose where the fog starts, and turn off the item name over the hotbar. On both loaders, with nothing else to install.

## ⚠️ Important Notes

- **The zoom key is C by default**, like OptiFine. Minecraft also uses C for "Save Hotbar Activator", which only works in creative and combined with a number key. If that gets in the way, change either one in Options → Controls → Key Binds, under "Borderless Window"
- Every other setting stays as it was, and every new option starts at Minecraft's own behavior. The zoom does nothing until you press its key
- When updating, delete the 1.9.0 jar from your mods folder

## ✨ New Features

### Zoom

- **Press C to zoom in**, 4× by default. The key is in Minecraft's Controls, in its own "Borderless Window" category
- **Hold or Toggle**: zoom only while the key is held down, or press once to zoom in and again to zoom out
- **Scroll to Zoom**: while zooming, the mouse wheel zooms further in or back out, from 1× to 50×, instead of changing the hotbar slot. It follows Minecraft's Discrete Scrolling and Scroll Sensitivity. Every new zoom starts again at the Zoom Level
- **Zoom Level**: from 2× to 16×
- **Smooth Zoom**: eases in and out of the zoom, at any frame rate. Turn it off to jump straight in
- **Hide Hand** while zooming (on by default) and **Hide HUD** while zooming (off by default), the latter just like pressing F1
- **The mouse turns slower in proportion to the zoom**, so the crosshair moves across the world at the same speed as without zoom
- It only narrows the field of view: nothing is drawn any farther away, and it stacks with your FOV and the mod's FOV sliders
- **The spyglass is left alone**: while you look through one, the zoom steps aside and the mouse wheel goes back to the hotbar
- The options are a new **Zoom** group on the Camera page in Sodium, and a new section in the mod's config screen

### Sky and weather

Options Minecraft does not have, from OptiFine's Details menu. All three are on by default and only change what is drawn:

- **Sun and Moon**: hide them. Day still turns into night, and sunrises and sunsets keep their colors
- **Stars**: hide them for a plain night sky
- With shaders, packs that draw their own sun, moon and stars keep them; those are set in the pack. Rain and snow are hidden with shaders too
- **Rain and Snow**: hide the falling rain and snow. It still rains for mobs, crops and fishing, and the rain sounds and splashes stay
- A new **Sky and Weather** group on the Visual Effects page, after the clouds

### Fog start

- **Fog Start**, like OptiFine's: choose where the distance fog begins, from 1% to 95% of your render distance. **Default (~90%)** keeps Minecraft's own. Lower values give a softer, deeper haze
- Only the ordinary terrain fog moves. The Nether's thick fog, water, lava, Blindness and Darkness are left alone. It is greyed out while Terrain Fog is off

### Held item name

- **Held Item Name**: turn off the item name that appears above the hotbar when you switch slots (OptiFine's "Held Item Tooltips"). On the General page, in a new **HUD** group

## 🔧 Technical Changes

- The zoom multiplies the value `GameRenderer.getFov` returns, after NeoForge's ComputeFov event. The held item's own FOV is left out, so the hand never gets magnified
- The key and the animation are read once per frame, so a press shows on the very next frame
- On Fabric, the key is registered through `fabric-key-binding-api-v1`, bundled inside the jar like the resource loader. Fabric API is still not required
- Fog start changes the depth of the fog band in the one branch of `FogRenderer.setupFog` that computes it, so no other fog can be touched. It is a single mixin for both loaders, and NeoForge's RenderFog event sees the moved start

# Borderless Window 1.8.0 *NeoForge 1.21.1 · 2026-11-08* > **The game rests when you are not looking.** Three new background options join the Unfocused FPS Limit on their own page, Minecraft's glint and menu blur sliders come back to Sodium's video settings, and every slider now moves in steps of 1. ## ⚠️ Important Notes - Every option keeps its ID, so existing settings carry over untouched. It is a share of your Master Volume, from 0 (Muted) to 100%, the default. Full volume returns as soon as you click back in, and sounds that start while muted (music, ambient loops) are there when you return - **Pause Rendering When Minimized**: stops drawing frames while the window is minimized and slows the game loop to 10 FPS. The game itself keeps running — the world, sounds and multiplayer connections are unaffected; only the picture stops until you restore the window. Off by default - **Idle FPS Limit**: after a number of minutes with no keyboard or mouse input (1 to 30, Off by default), the frame rate is capped at a value you choose (5 to 60 FPS, 30 by default) — even while the window is focused. releases.notes:
# 1.7.0

## Unfocused FPS limit

- New **Unfocused FPS Limit**: caps the frame rate while the game window is not focused — after Alt+Tab, while minimized, or with another window or monitor in front. Off by default, then 5 to 60 FPS in steps of 5
- Minecraft 1.21.1 keeps rendering at full speed in the background, burning GPU power and heat on frames nobody sees. 1.21.2 later added its own limit; this brings the same idea to 1.21.1
- It can only lower the frame rate: a regular Max Framerate that is already lower still wins, and menus with no world loaded keep Minecraft's own 60 FPS. The cap lifts on the very next frame after you click back into the game
- With **Dynamic FPS** installed the option steps aside and is greyed out, with a tooltip saying why. Both mods hook the same methods, and two settings fighting over one behavior would only be confusing — Dynamic FPS covers this and more

## Draw distances

- Four new sliders that stop drawing things past a distance you choose: **Dropped Items**, **Experience Orbs**, **Armor Stands** and **Particles**. Every slider starts at **Default** on the left, which keeps Minecraft's own distance
- Minecraft draws items up to 16 blocks away and orbs up to 32 (both scaled by its Entity Distance option), armor stands as far as the server sends them, and spawns particles up to 32 blocks away. These sliders can only lower those numbers
- It is purely visual: items and orbs are only hidden, never removed. Items can still be picked up, orbs still fly to you, and nothing changes for the server or other players
- **Glowing** entities are always drawn, since the outline is information meant to be seen from afar
- **Armor stands with a visible name** are always drawn: servers and adventure maps use them as floating text and holograms
- Particles are refused when they would spawn, which is where their cost is, rather than hidden while they already exist. Particles the game marks as always visible are left alone, exactly as Minecraft does with its own 32-block limit

## Sodium integration

- The mod's section went from nine pages to four: **General** (F11, FPS overlay and unfocused limit, enchantment numerals), **Visual Effects** (fog, clouds, screen overlays), **Camera** (bobbing, FOV, distortion) and **Distances**. Inside each page the features are split into groups, the same way Sodium's own General page does it
- Every option keeps its ID, so existing settings carry over untouched
- The no-Sodium config screen follows the same order, keeping its per-feature headers

## Internal

- New `distance/` package; `fps/` gains `UnfocusedFpsState`
- New mixins: `MinecraftMixin` (`getFramerateLimit`), `EntityRenderDispatcherMixin` (`shouldRender`) and `LevelRendererMixin` (`addParticleInternal`). Sodium's entity culling wraps the frustum test one call deeper, inside `EntityRenderer.shouldRender`, so the two stack cleanly
- New generic `IntOptionSlider` for the no-Sodium screen: a stepped integer slider with the label supplied by the caller. Arrow keys move one whole step instead of vanilla's one pixel
- New `build.yml` workflow: builds every push and pull request to `master` and keeps the jar as an artifact for 14 days. A commit message containing `[curseforge]` also uploads that build to CurseForge
- Dependabot now keeps the workflow actions up to date

# 1.6.1

- Fixed Portal Distortion not applying after crossing a Nether portal. You arrive standing inside the destination portal, but Minecraft ignores that portal until its cooldown runs out, so with a Nausea effect active the distortion switched to the Nausea percentage while you were still in the portal. Stepping out and back in was the only way to get the portal percentage back. Touching a portal now always counts as the portal, cooldown or not
- Corrected the 1.6.0 notes about the green nausea texture. It is not left to vanilla: Nausea Distortion drives it the same way Minecraft's own Distortion Effects slider does, so lowering Nausea Distortion trades the spinning for the green cue, and at 0% there is no spinning and the texture is at full strength. While a portal is the source, the texture follows Minecraft's slider only. The code always behaved this way; only the notes were wrong

## Internal

- New `EntityMixin` records contact with a Nether portal at the head of `setAsInsidePortal`, before vanilla's cooldown check, and `LocalPlayerMixin` counts that contact as the portal when attributing the distortion source

mods.description: Adds borderless fullscreen to Minecraft with a 3-mode system (Windowed / Borderless / Fullscreen) and configurable F11 behavior, plus a growing set of video and quality-of-life options Minecraft doesn't expose. Every setting defaults to vanilla behavior. Optional Sodium video settings integration. Configurable from the Mods menu, no dependencies required.

releases.notes:
# 1.6.0

## Camera overlays

- Added four toggles for the full-screen overlays Minecraft draws over your view: **Pumpkin**, **Freeze**, **Portal** and **Spyglass**
- **Pumpkin Overlay** removes the blur drawn while wearing a carved pumpkin, so it can be worn against endermen without the visual cost. Helmet overlays added by other mods are never affected
- **Freeze Overlay** removes the frost border drawn while freezing in powder snow. That border also warns you are taking freeze damage; the frozen hearts on the HUD still show it
- **Portal Overlay** removes the purple warp drawn while standing inside a Nether portal, which mostly gets in the way while building or aligning them
- **Spyglass Overlay** removes the scope texture and the black bars. The zoom itself is unchanged — only the frame around it is removed
- All four live in the existing Screen Overlays section, alongside the water and fire toggles
- The vignette is deliberately not offered: it doubles as the world border warning, and a plain toggle would delete that warning along with the darkening

## Field of view

- Minecraft has one **FOV Effects** slider for every source at once. It is now split into four: **Speed**, **Flying**, **Bow** and **Fluid**, each 0-100% with 100% being vanilla
- **Speed FOV** is the one worth having: with Speed potions or a modified movement attribute the FOV never settles, and until now there was no way to soften that without removing the bow zoom too
- **Flying FOV** covers creative flight only. Elytra gliding is a different thing and is not affected
- **Bow FOV** keeps the same easing curve and only changes how deep the zoom goes. The spyglass is never touched: its zoom is what the item does, not a visual effect
- **Fluid FOV** is the squeeze applied underwater and in lava
- All four sit under Minecraft's own FOV Effects slider rather than replacing it — with that at Off, nothing here has any effect

## Distortion

- Minecraft has one **Distortion Effects** slider covering both the Nether portal and the Nausea effect. It is now split into **Portal Distortion** and **Nausea Distortion**, each 0-100%
- The two share one accumulator internally, so the source is attributed per tick from the rate vanilla itself picks. Walking into a portal while under a Nausea potion correctly applies the portal percentage, and applies the Nausea one again the moment you step out
- Both sit under Minecraft's own Distortion Effects slider, same as the FOV options
- The green nausea texture is left entirely to vanilla. It is Minecraft's accessibility trade — a static cue that replaces the spinning as you lower *its* slider — and driving it from ours turned "less motion" into a bright green full-screen overlay, which is the opposite of what the option is for

## Sodium integration

- Two vanilla sliders Sodium's video settings leave out are now available inside the mod's pages: **Distortion Effects (Minecraft)** and **FOV Effects (Minecraft)**, each at the top of the page it governs so the hierarchy reads top-down
- Both are the same settings found in Minecraft's Accessibility Settings and are saved with Minecraft's options, not the mod's
- The Sodium section now has nine per-feature pages: General, FPS Overlay, Fog, Clouds, Screen Overlays, Bobbing, FOV, Distortion and Enchantment Style
- Every option remains fully available without Sodium via the Mods menu Config screen, except the two vanilla sliders above — without Sodium those are one click away in Minecraft's own menus and duplicating them would serve nobody

## Internal

- New `fov/` and `distortion/` packages; `screeneffect/` gains `CameraOverlayFilter`
- New mixins: `GuiMixin`, `AbstractClientPlayerMixin`, `LocalPlayerMixin`
- The camera overlays need bytecode rather than an event: NeoForge exposes the whole group as a single `CAMERA_OVERLAYS` GUI layer, so cancelling it would remove all of them at once. The pumpkin and freeze overlays share one vanilla method and are told apart by texture

releases.notes:
# 1.5.0 — Enchantment level numerals

Enchantment levels above X showed raw text instead of a number: a
Looting 11 book read "Looting enchantment.level.11". Levels are legal
all the way to 255, but Minecraft only ships names for the first ten.

This fixes it and adds a style option with three values:

- Mixed (default): Roman numerals up to X, plain numbers past it. This
  is the fix on its own — nothing you already see changes.
- Always Roman: generated numerals at every level, XI through CCLV.
- Always Numbers: plain numbers at every level, including 1-10.

Mixed defers to the language file whenever a translation exists, so
resource packs that do name high levels keep working. The other two are
explicit choices and always generate.

Implementation: WrapOperation (MixinExtras) wraps the single
Component.translatable call inside Enchantment.getFullname, capturing
the target method's own level parameter instead of parsing it back out
of the key. The guard above that call is untouched, so single-level
enchantments like Mending still show no number, and returning the
original Operation leaves vanilla's component identical whenever no
override applies. One injection covers item tooltips, enchanted books
and the enchanting table.

New enchantment/ package (EnchantmentLevelStyle, EnchantmentLevelState,
EnchantmentLevelFormatter) plus mixin/EnchantmentMixin, wired into both
UIs, the config file and the three lang files.
